description: Long narrow charcoal brazier on legs with a row of grilling pork skewers and a bag of sticky rice hung from a side hook.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Long narrow charcoal brazier on four steel legs, a close row of grilling meat skewers laid across the open trough, a hooked steel arm on one end with a hanging plastic bag of sticky rice, small ash drawer beneath Materials: Soot-blackened steel trough with grey ash and glowing charcoal, rust-pitted legs, charred bamboo skewer ends, caramelised glaze on the meat, cloudy stretched plastic bag.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,920/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas.

featureReviews.evidence: Built 0.934 x 0.857 x 0.459 m against the declared 0.90 x 0.85 x 0.44 (+3.8 / +0.8 / +4.3%); drum rim 0.60, drum bottom 0.415, drawer 0.345-0.445, crook 0.848, bag 0.295-0.70, legs splayed to +-0.40 -- the plate's stations, hook and bag on the LEFT as the plate shows; skewer handles overhang the rear rod as in the plate.
featureReviews.notes: Third build: the second build's trough sat 6 cm too high with a leg brace the plate does not have; rebuilt from the plate mask, not the proxy, which fused three legs into one.

featureReviews.evidence: Twenty instanced 0.36 m skewers at 20 mm pitch, meat massed on the front half in three tones with char scraps, bamboo handles overhanging the rear rod, jittered in x/y/z/pitch/yaw/roll by index.
featureReviews.notes: Meat pieces are flattened boxes; the plate's are rounder. Second build had fourteen 0.34 m sticks with three cubes each and no overhang.

featureReviews.evidence: Soot-black drum at the plate's luma 40 with folded lips, solid end plates and a rear rod; rusty L-angle legs; drawer housing with proud front and handle; round-bar crook; translucent bag (0.68) with a knot over a rice ellipsoid; ash slab with 22 charcoal / ash / ember chunks and two ember strips.
featureReviews.notes: Rust patina on the legs is a vertex tone, not a patterned tile: a multiply cannot lighten soot to rust, and the ash bed shares the material so envelope re-basing was not available.

name: Moo Ping Skewer Brazier
nameTh: เตาย่างหมูปิ้ง
notes: Budget class overridden from medium to large. At 0.9 m the size rule says medium, which allows 2 draw calls and 2 materials, and this prop needs three distinct surfaces that cannot share one: the sooty steel brazier, the charred bamboo-and-meat skewer row, and the translucent plastic rice bag. The skewer row laid across the open trough is the entire silhouette and is what makes it read as moo ping rather than as a generic firebox, so it cannot be collapsed into the brazier material. Deliberately a standing brazier on legs, not a wheeled cart -- a cart-shaped grill is a different prop. No destruction groups: it is a static street-side prop, not a breakable. Depth corrected 0.35 -> 0.44 on the third build (2026-09-01): the plate's drum is ~0.31 across and its skewer handles overhang the rear rim by ~0.10 (bamboo 0.36 long with 0.14 of meat over the coals), so the real footprint is drum plus overhang, 0.44; the splayed feet reach +-0.185. Width and height stand at 0.90 x 0.85.
